text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Interior ministry parliamentary commission unanimously approves draft law on regionalisation.
- Food exhibition in Casablanca mirrors performance of agro-industry sector which represents 20 percent of industrial exports and annual turnover of 7 billion dirhams ($744 million).
- Morocco to host two-day international forum on water from March 21 in Marrakesh.
- United Nations Security Council says no progress on implementation of referendum in Western Sahara.
- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak expected in Morocco for meeting with King Hassan over peace process in the Middle East.
- London-based Arabic newspaper Al Hayat says Spain considers proposing to Morocco 99 years joint sovereignty over the two enclaves of Ceuta and Melilla, held by Spain since the 16th century.
- Finance and public works ministers fly to Kuwait and Saudi Arabia in attempt to lure investors.
- Morocco and Spain to reinforce cooperation on education.
- French TV channel Canal plus Horizons says it plans to get 30,000 Moroccan viewers by 1998.
- Economic car launched by Italian maker FIAT last year marked pickup of car industry. New cars gradually replace second-hand vehicles which used to dominate the market.
